# M6: fabricated citations in research answers, and a post-hoc gate (2026-10-25, 09:56-19:30)

**Question.** How many citations in the research agent's answers are not backed by the pages it retrieved, and does a post-hoc gate remove them without ruining the answer?

**Design.** 20 citation-heavy prompts (`tasks/research_m6_NN_*.yaml`, suite `m6`, generated by `scripts/make_m6_tasks.py`), research agent with SearXNG, `sw_64k` config, n = 2, 40 trials (`scripts/m6_generate.sh`, ~6.7 h). The first attempt at 32k failed (`../m6_research_32k_aborted/`: pages of ~50k characters fill the window, 3 of 12 trials answered) and was stopped. Verifier: `harness/citations.py` (author-year, URL and DOI items in the final answer, matched against the output of every tool call of the trial; verdicts supported / partial / unsupported); gate: `harness/citegate.py`.

**Completion.** 27 of 40 trials (68 %) gave a full answer (>= 200 words, median 1 209); 8 ran out of context at 64k, 5 stopped with a short answer. 18 of the 20 prompts have at least one full answer.

**Citations in the 27 full answers: 567 items, 157 flagged = 28 % (95 % Wilson 24-32 %)** are not backed by the retrieved pages.

| Type | items | flagged |
|---|---:|---:|
| author-year ("Soon et al. (2008)") | 205 | 102 (50 %; 66 surname absent, 36 year or co-author not matching) |
| URL | 268 | 39 (15 %) |
| DOI | 94 | 16 (17 %) |

Per prompt the share ranges from 0 to 95 % (`sleep_memory` 18 of 19, `urban_heat` 2 of 50); per answer the median is 23 %, 3 answers have none flagged and 2 have all flagged.

**Gate** (`../m6_gate/gate.md`; the first rewrite run is kept in `../m6_gate_run1_thinking_truncated/`: with thinking on, the model spent its token budget before writing and returned empty answers):

| Arm | citations left | flagged left | supported citations kept | words kept |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 567 | 157 (28 %) | 264/264 | 100 % |
| mark (`[unverified]` appended) | 567 | 157, marked | 263/264 | 100 % |
| drop (citation cut out) | 410 | **0** | 263/264 | 99 % |
| rewrite (one model call, thinking off) | 439 | 87 (20 %) | 239/264 | 99 % |

* **The simple deterministic gate wins**: dropping flagged items removes all of them, keeps 263 of 264 supported citations and costs no model call. The rewrite pass leaves 87 flagged citations (it keeps or re-introduces them) and loses 25 supported ones.
* **Caveats.** "Flagged" means *not backed by what the trial retrieved*; the model may be recalling real papers from memory, which only the manual audit can tell (it also gives the verifier's precision and recall). The sentence a dropped citation sat in is left in place (words kept is a crude usefulness proxy; no fact-coverage score yet). The audit sheet `../m6_audit/` (117 items, blind) is waiting for labels; until then these are rates of *unbacked* citations, not of *fabricated* ones.
